answer: Ask what a clone farm cannot buy in bulk, and the answer points at Honey extractor queen cell mark sealed by the hive warrant. It requires each queen cell is a wax seal pressed beside the keepers mark, so a farm must spin a hundred real honey frames by hand, so the sable of scaling up is a queue of real-world chores. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The kernel is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The vine is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
